correctness.rationale: Each \(\ell_p^2\) block and its conjugate dual are finite-dimensional strictly convex and smooth. Their \(\ell_2\)-sums have LUR and Gâteaux smooth norms; LUR follows from convergence of the block-length vectors and finite-dimensional strict convexity with a small-tail argument. Uniform block norm inequalities yield \(\|z\|_X\le\|z\|_H\le\sqrt2\|z\|_X\). In any LUR real Banach space, a fixed vector cannot have reverse support evaluations tending to one along Birkhoff–James orthogonal unit vectors: the near-unit norming evaluation forces convergence to the positive or negative fixed point by LUR, contradicting the orthogonality separation \(\|a\pm b\|\ge1\). The explicit \(p\)-block pair \(u_p=(1,t)/(1+t^p)^{1/p}\), \(v_p=(-t^{p-1},1)/(1+t^{p(p-1)})^{1/p}\), \(t=1-p^{-1/2}\), satisfies \(j(u_p)(v_p)=0\) exactly and \(j(v_p)(u_p)=r_p\to1\) with \(\sqrt p(1-r_p)\to1\). Embedding each pair in one block proves global supremum one; strict convexity prevents attainment. Reflexive smooth strict-convex duality interchanges directions and transfers the same witness to \(X^*\). The inspected verifier tests exact cancellation at square exponents and asymptotic scaling but does not prove the infinite-dimensional properties.

value.rationale: The simultaneous pointwise/global symmetry separation for a well-controlled Hilbert renorming and its dual is a natural Banach space geometric counterexample. The nonattained extremal defect and precise rate distinguish it from a merely smooth counterexample, and both local directions are explicitly controlled.

final_claim: For \(X=(\bigoplus_{n\ge1}\ell_{n+2}^2)_{\ell_2}\), an equivalent norm on real Hilbert sequence space with distortion at most \(\sqrt2\), both \(X\) and \(X^*\) are separable, reflexive, Gâteaux smooth and locally uniformly rotund. Every nonzero point is individually left- and right-\(C\)-approximately symmetric for Birkhoff–James orthogonality, yet the global \(C\)-symmetry defects satisfy \(\sigma_C(X)=\sigma_C(X^*)=1\), with no attaining pair and with explicit witness deficit asymptotic \(1-r_p\sim p^{-1/2}\).
limitations: The norm is Hilbert-equivalent, not the usual Hilbert norm; it is not uniformly convex.
The 2018 full paper documenting an earlier smooth example could not be verified in full; possible overlap of enhanced LUR/dual/local features remains a literature risk.
